title: Simplified Aircraft Motion — Forces in One Direction
learningObjectives: Explain that steady level motion corresponds to balanced opposing forces while unbalanced forces cause acceleration
Calculate acceleration from net force and mass using a = F_net/m
Interpret net force as the difference between an opposing pair such as thrust minus drag or lift minus weight

sources.title: Simplified Aircraft Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

explanations.text: In simplified one-dimensional analysis, motion in a single direction is studied while opposite forces are treated as balanced. When paired forces cancel, the model can maintain steady velocity.

evidence.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust

explanations.text: When forces become unbalanced the object accelerates in the direction of the greater force, with the acceleration determined by dividing the net force by the mass.

evidence.quote: If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

explanations.text: Net force in the chosen direction is the difference between the two opposing forces in that direction and is the F used to find acceleration.

evidence.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.
Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

behavioralTests.name: zero net force maintains no acceleration
positive thrust minus drag accelerates forward
